messages:

Cc: Tom Brooks <tomb@cascadehealth.io>

Subject: Sudden latency + errors after model v2.1 roll — urgent

Hi Monica / Markus,

We started seeing a sharp spike in P95 latency and a noticeable uptick in model errors (response truncation and malformed JSON) about 15 minutes after Redwood pushed the v2.1 quant profile to our dedicated pool. Key metrics:
- P95 latency: 1.2s -> 2.9s
- Error rate (500/timeout): 0.2% -> 3.8%
- Throughput: sustained drop of ~22% for our peak request mixes

This is impacting live triage workflows. I've attached a small PNG of the latency curve and an excerpt of error logs. Please escalate — we have a major care-batch running this afternoon.

Relevant context: we pinned the model to redwood-llama-7b:v2026-05-29 but allowed the recommended quant profile to be applied (auto-quant: true).

Can you confirm rollback options and expected timeline?

Thanks,
Elena
Director, ML Ops
CascadeHealth

Date: Sat, 30 May 2026 10:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden latency + errors after model v2.1 roll — investigation notes

Quick technical summary from the pool-side checks:
- We saw increased token generation time correlated with the v2.1 quant profile when sequence-lengths exceed ~512 tokens. The quant changes adjust kernel paths and post-fusion schedules which appear to regress perf for the mix Cascade sends (longer prompts + heavy system prompt).
- Error types point to timeouts in the streaming handler and occasional KV cache misses leading to fallback serialization that trips our validation layer (hence malformed JSON).
- Config diff (attached) shows v2.1 enabled "kv_cache_prefetch": true and a changed GEMM kernel selector.

Immediate actions taken:
1) Scoped the affected pool and disabled auto-quant for Cascade's dedicated instances.
2) Initiated a rollback to v2.0 quant profile for the pool (in-progress).
3) Increased per-request CPU leash and extended streaming timeouts to mitigate malformed JSON while rollback proceeds.

Estimated ETA for rollback completion: 45–70 minutes from 10:22AM PT. Will monitor and post metrics to JIRA-CH-712.

Notes for postmortem: quantify request mix, add targeted microbenchmarks for sequences >512, and update model catalog perf note about v2.1 behavior for long contexts.

— Sean
Senior SRE, Inference Runtime

Attachments: prod-config-diff.patch (text)

- Customer impact: live workflows affected; estimated revenue exposure for the afternoon batch ~ $14k in deferred transactions and high-risk patient workflows.
- Technical status: Sean executed rollback; metrics trending back to baseline but still validating edge-cases.

2) Temporary service credit for affected capacity window.
3) A written plan to avoid recurrence (test harness + gated rollout for quant changes).

I propose we offer: 5% credit for the impacted month + priority placement on our next round of perf testing with their key prompt-set. Rishi — please advise if we should escalate to a higher commercial make-goods.

Markus
VP, Customer Success (Acting)

Subject: Final: rollback complete + next steps (CH incident CH-712)

Elena / Tom — thank you for patience.

Summary: rollback to v2.0 quant profile completed at 16:12 PT. Post-rollback metrics (15m window):
- P95 latency: returned to 1.25s (within normal variance)
- Error rate: down to 0.3%
- Throughput: recovered to within 98% of baseline

Attached: condensed incident notes and the prod-config-diff we used to validate the rollback. We're opening a formal RCA JIRA (JIRA-CH-712) that will include:
- Root cause analysis (quant scheduling mismatch with long-context kernel)
- Remediation: gated rollout for quant changes, additional microbenchmarks for long-sequence workloads, and opt-in auto-quant flags exposed to dedicated customers.
- Commercial: Markus proposed 5% credit for the impacted capacity window; I will coordinate with finance and legal and follow up with a credit memo draft by EOD Monday.

Immediate asks for Cascade: please confirm if your team wants extended monitoring for the next 48 hours and if you'd like a dedicated postmortem session (we can schedule 60 minutes next week).

Apologies again for the disruption — we take this seriously and will publish a detailed RCA when complete.

— Monica
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
